title: Asking a compiled selector to print its structure never returns
text_original:
- Ensure custom selectors or namespace dictionaries reject non-string keys
- Fix handling of `:in-range` and `:out-of-range` with end of year weeks
- Fix a potential infinite loop in pretty printing of compiled selector objects
text_rewritten:
When a selector does not match what we expect, our first debugging step is to ask the compiled selector to print its own structure. For positional selectors such as :nth-child(...) and :nth-of-type(...), and for attribute selectors, that call never comes back: the process sits at full CPU until we kill it, and whatever else the script was doing is lost. Other selector kinds print fine, including :lang(...), class selectors, plain tag selectors and text-containment selectors, so it is not the printing itself that is broken.

The dump should always terminate and describe the selector it was given, whatever the selector happens to contain.

When a selector does not match what we expect, our first debugging step is to ask the compiled selector to print its own structure. For positional selectors such as :nth-child(...) and :nth-of-type(...), and for attribute selectors, that call never comes back: the process sits at full CPU until we kill it, and whatever else the script was doing is lost. Other selector kinds print fine, including :lang(...), class selectors, plain tag selectors and text-containment selectors, so it is not the printing itself that is broken.

The dump should always terminate and describe the selector it was given, whatever the selector happens to contain.
acceptance_hint: Printing the structure of any compiled selector, positional and attribute selectors included, terminates and produces a rendering that mentions the selector's own values.
